package_info.why_malicious: The entire package set is malicious because they were mass-published with the sole purpose of distributing phishing links via package metadata (descriptions), luring users to credential-harvesting and scam sites, and boosting the SEO of phishing infrastructure. No legitimate code or functionality is provided.

execution_context.trigger: package metadata parsing (install-time, search-time, or when viewing package details)
execution_context.file_location: package description field (e.g., .nuspec, package.json, setup.py metadata)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user or automated system views the package description (during install, search, or browsing), the description displays enticing phishing links that direct the user to external phishing sites, leading to credential theft or scam.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding external, unrelated URLs in package metadata is a classic phishing and SEO abuse tactic, especially when the links promise cheats, free resources, or rewards.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package descriptions provide documentation or usage instructions, not external links to unrelated, suspicious domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to documentation or project homepages, but not to unrelated 'free code' or 'hack' sites.
key_indicators: Presence of external URLs in description
Links to known phishing or scam domains

attack_chain.action: Automated creation of thousands of packages with enticing names and phishing links in descriptions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages appear in search results and are indexed by search engines.

attack_chain.action: User or automated system views package details, sees phishing link in description.

attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, scam, or referral reward for attacker.

attack_chain.action: Some phishing sites redirect to eCommerce with referral IDs, generating financial rewards for attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives referral bonuses or store credit.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing external URLs unrelated to the package's stated functionality
Descriptions promising cheats, hacks, free codes, or followers
Mass publication of similarly named packages with only metadata changes
file_indicators: Package metadata fields (description, readme) containing suspicious URLs
network_indicators: and 80+ other domains listed in the report
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package metadata (description, readme) for external URLs, especially those matching known phishing or scam domains, or using enticement language. Flag packages with no functional code and only external links. Monitor for mass-published packages with similar naming patterns and descriptions. Cross-reference URLs against threat intelligence feeds.
